subproblem.title: A flat-Cauchy subsequence from total boundedness (Simon Ch. 6, 7.2, (5))
subproblem.statement: Assume the following proposition. (IS) [conjunct (c) of the frozen statement of cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub] For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and IM A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), the current A − B is IM. Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and X_j ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) (j ∈ ℕ). Suppose that for every η ∈ (0, ∞] there is a finite set 𝒬 ⊆ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) such that for every j there are Q ∈ 𝒬 and integer multiplicity R ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(U), S ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) with X_j − Q − S = ∂R and M(R) + M(S) ≤ η. Then there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ such that for every r ∈ ℕ there are integer multiplicity R_r ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(U), S_r ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) with X_{φ(r+1)} − X_{φ(r)} − S_r = ∂R_r and M(R_r) + M(S_r) ≤ 2^{−r} (that is, (2⁻¹)^r in [0, ∞]). Conventions: 𝒟_d(U) is the space of d-currents in U (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U d) and 𝒟^d(U) the test d-forms in U (TestFormOn U d: smooth forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U); |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector (covectorEuclideanNorm); M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of max(X(ω), 0) over ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (such ω are called admissible for M_G), and M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X) for X ∈ 𝒟_d(U); spt is the support of Simon 6.2.11 (GeometricCurrentOn.support); IM means integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity), an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) is the contract structure IMRep with R.measure = θ·Hⁿ⌞M, R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ (⟨ω, ξ⟩ := ξ(x)(ω(x))) and R represents X when X(ω) = R.action(ω) for all test forms ω; subtraction of currents is the contract instance Sub; X ⇀ Y is WeaklyConvergesOn.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (A B : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity A → IsIntegerMultiplicity B → IsIntegerMultiplicity (A - B)) → ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (X : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), IsOpen U → (∀ η : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < η → ∃ 𝒬 : Set (GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), 𝒬.Finite ∧ ∀ j, ∃ Q ∈ 𝒬, ∃ (R : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 2)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), IsIntegerMultiplicity R ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity S ∧ X j - Q - S = R.boundary ∧ R.mass + S.mass ≤ η) → ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ r, ∃ (R : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 2)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), IsIntegerMultiplicity R ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity S ∧ X (φ (r + 1)) - X (φ r) - S = R.boundary ∧ R.mass + S.mass ≤ (2⁻¹ : ℝ≥0∞) ^ r
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 7.2, "apply (1) with ε = 1, 1/2, 1/4 etc. to extract a subsequence … d_W̃(T_{j_{r+1}}, T_{j_r}) < 2^{−r}", i.e. steps 4–5 of the parent proof (pigeonhole on the finite family and nested infinite index sets).
1. (F1) Mass subadditivity: for currents A, B with the same domain and every set G, M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B). Indeed, if ω is admissible for M_G then so is −ω, (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) + B(−ω), and ENNReal.ofReal(s + t) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(s) + ENNReal.ofReal(t); take the supremum over ω.
2. (Close pairs.) Call indices j, l η-close if there are IM R ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(U), S ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) with X_j − X_l − S = ∂R and M(R) + M(S) ≤ η. Claim: if for one current Q we have X_j − Q − S_j = ∂R_j and X_l − Q − S_l = ∂R_l with IM R_j, R_l, S_j, S_l, M(R_j) + M(S_j) ≤ η and M(R_l) + M(S_l) ≤ η, then j and l are 2η-close. Put R := R_j − R_l and S := S_j − S_l, IM by (IS) (U is open). For ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U): (X_j − X_l − S)(ω) = (X_j(ω) − Q(ω) − S_j(ω)) − (X_l(ω) − Q(ω) − S_l(ω)) = R_j(dω) − R_l(dω) = R(dω) = ∂R(ω); hence X_j − X_l − S = ∂R (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). By (F1), M(R) + M(S) ≤ M(R_j) + M(R_l) + M(S_j) + M(S_l) ≤ 2η.
3. (Infinite pigeonhole.) Let η ∈ (0, ∞] and let I ⊆ ℕ be infinite. Take the finite set 𝒬 given by the hypothesis for η, and for each j ∈ I choose Q_j ∈ 𝒬 together with a decomposition X_j − Q_j − S_j = ∂R_j as in the hypothesis. Since I is infinite and 𝒬 finite, some fiber I' := {j ∈ I : Q_j = Q} is infinite (Mathlib Finite.exists_infinite_fiber). By step 2 any two j, l ∈ I' are 2η-close.
4. (Nested index sets.) Define infinite sets ℕ = I_0 ⊇ I_1 ⊇ I_2 ⊇ ⋯ recursively: given the infinite set I_r, step 3 with η := 2^{−(r+1)} yields an infinite I_{r+1} ⊆ I_r any two elements of which are 2^{−r}-close (2·2^{−(r+1)} = 2^{−r}).
5. (Diagonal choice.) Let φ(0) := an element of I_1, and given φ(r) ∈ I_{r+1}, let φ(r + 1) := an element of I_{r+2} with φ(r + 1) > φ(r) (it exists because I_{r+2} is infinite). Then φ is strictly increasing, φ(r) ∈ I_{r+1} and φ(r + 1) ∈ I_{r+2} ⊆ I_{r+1}, so φ(r + 1) and φ(r) are 2^{−r}-close: there are IM R_r, S_r with X_{φ(r+1)} − X_{φ(r)} − S_r = ∂R_r and M(R_r) + M(S_r) ≤ 2^{−r}. ∎
proof_key_steps: Two members decomposed against the same Q are 2η-close: subtract the decompositions, use (IS) and mass subadditivity.
Infinite pigeonhole on the finite family 𝒬 gives an infinite set of mutually 2η-close indices.
Nested infinite index sets for η = 2^{−(r+1)} and a diagonal choice make consecutive chosen indices 2^{−r}-close.

audit.reason: The statement requires no unstated IM hypothesis on X. Subtracting decompositions with a common center gives the correctly signed identity and doubled mass bound. Nested infinite fibers and the diagonal choice yield StrictMono and the exact bound (2⁻¹)^r.

subproblem.title: Choice of a good slicing level for a mass-bounded sequence of measures on ℝ
subproblem.statement: Let μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) be Borel measures on ℝ, let a < b be real numbers and let Λ ∈ [0, ∞) with μ_j([a, b]) ≤ Λ for every j. Then there are s ∈ ℝ with a < s < b, a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and C ∈ [0, ∞) such that (i) for every j, liminf_{h→0+} ENNReal.ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ_{φ(j)}((s − h, s)) ≤ C (limit inferior in [0, ∞] along h → 0 with h > 0, i.e. along 𝓝[>] 0); and (ii) for every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is δ > 0 such that μ_{φ(j)}([s − δ, s]) ≤ ε for all sufficiently large j.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (μ : ℕ → Measure ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (Λ : ℝ≥0∞), a < b → Λ ≠ ∞ → (∀ j, μ j (Icc a b) ≤ Λ) → ∃ (s : ℝ) (φ : ℕ → ℕ) (C : ℝ≥0∞), a < s ∧ s < b ∧ StrictMono φ ∧ C ≠ ∞ ∧ (∀ j, liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ (φ j) (Ioo (s - h) s)) (𝓝[>] 0) ≤ C) ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ᶠ j in atTop, μ (φ j) (Icc (s - δ) s) ≤ ε
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the choice of the slicing level s in step 3 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2, "by 4.5(1),(2) and an argument as in 6.7(2) of Ch. 2"), with the measures μ_j there pushed forward by g. The parent proof combines two ingredients: compactness of the mass-bounded measures with countability of the atoms of the limit, which yields no limiting mass at the level s; and measurable majorants of the slice quantity controlled by Fatou's lemma, which yields bounded slice masses. Mathlib's FiniteMeasure/Portmanteau files, SimonGMT's Chapter01 compactness theorem and Mathlib's DerivIntegrable file are not in the frozen import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission, so both ingredients are realized elementarily here. Compactness comes from Helly's selection argument (Tychonoff in a countable product, countably many discontinuities of a monotone function). The majorants are lim infs of difference quotients, controlled by Tonelli and Fatou.
0. (Reduction to [a, b].) Let ν_j := μ_j⌞[a, b], a finite Borel measure with ν_j(ℝ) ≤ Λ. If a < s < b, then (s − h, s) ⊆ [a, b] for 0 < h ≤ s − a and [s − δ, s] ⊆ [a, b] for 0 < δ ≤ s − a, and on subsets of [a, b] the measures μ_j and ν_j agree. The limit inferior in (i) along 𝓝[>] 0 only depends on the values for h ∈ (0, s − a). Hence it suffices to find s, φ, C such that (i) holds for ν in place of μ and (ii) holds for ν with some δ ∈ (0, s − a].
1. (Helly selection.) Let (d_i)_{i∈ℕ} enumerate the countable nonempty set D := ℚ ∩ (a, b), which is dense in (a, b) (Mathlib exists_rat_btwn). For each j put v_j := (ν_j([a, d_i]).toReal)_{i∈ℕ} ∈ (ℕ → ℝ). Every v_j lies in the set Π_i [0, Λ.toReal], which is compact by Tychonoff (Mathlib isCompact_univ_pi), and ℕ → ℝ is first countable (a countable product of metric spaces). By Mathlib IsCompact.tendsto_subseq there are a strictly increasing φ₁ and G = (G_i)_i ∈ Π_i [0, Λ.toReal] with v_{φ₁(j)} → G, i.e. (Mathlib tendsto_pi_nhds) ν_{φ₁(j)}([a, d_i]).toReal → G_i for every i. If d_i ≤ d_k then ν_j([a, d_i]) ≤ ν_j([a, d_k]) for all j, hence G_i ≤ G_k.
2. (Limit distribution function.) Define G̃ : ℝ → ℝ by G̃(t) := sup({0} ∪ {G_i : d_i < t}), the supremum of a nonempty set bounded above by Λ.toReal. G̃ is nondecreasing, so its set N₁ of discontinuity points is countable (Mathlib Monotone.countable_not_continuousAt), hence Lebesgue-null. Moreover (α) G_i ≤ G̃(t) whenever d_i < t; and (β) G̃(t) ≤ G_i whenever t < d_i, because every element of the set defining G̃(t) is either 0 ≤ G_i or some G_k with d_k < t < d_i, so G_k ≤ G_i.
3. (No concentration at continuity points of G̃.) Claim: if s ∈ (a, b) ∖ N₁, then for every real ε > 0 there is δ ∈ (0, s − a] with ν_{φ₁(j)}([s − δ, s]) < ENNReal.ofReal(ε) for all large j. Indeed, by continuity of G̃ at s choose η > 0 with 2η < s − a, s + η < b and |G̃(t) − G̃(s)| < ε/2 whenever |t − s| ≤ 2η. By density of D choose i₁, i₂ with s − 2η < d_{i₁} < s − η and s < d_{i₂} < s + η. By (β) and (α), G̃(s − 2η) ≤ G_{i₁} and G_{i₂} ≤ G̃(s + η), so G_{i₂} − G_{i₁} ≤ G̃(s + η) − G̃(s − 2η) < ε. Put δ := η. Then [s − δ, s] ⊆ (d_{i₁}, d_{i₂}] ⊆ [a, b], and since [a, d_{i₂}] is the disjoint union of [a, d_{i₁}] and (d_{i₁}, d_{i₂}] (all of finite measure), ν_j([s − δ, s]) ≤ ν_j((d_{i₁}, d_{i₂}]) = ENNReal.ofReal(ν_j([a, d_{i₂}]).toReal − ν_j([a, d_{i₁}]).toReal). Along j ↦ φ₁(j) the real number in the last expression tends to G_{i₂} − G_{i₁} < ε, so it is < ε for all large j, which proves the claim.
4. (Measurable majorants of the slice quantity.) For j, n ∈ ℕ and t ∈ ℝ put h_n := 1/(n + 1), Q_{j,n}(t) := (n + 1)·ν_{φ₁(j)}((t − h_n, t)) ∈ [0, ∞] and q_j(t) := liminf_n Q_{j,n}(t). For fixed j and n, t ↦ ν_{φ₁(j)}((t − h_n, t)) is measurable, being the ν_{φ₁(j)}-measure of the t-section of the Borel set {(t, x) ∈ ℝ × ℝ : t − h_n < x < t} (Mathlib measurable_measure_prodMk_left; ν_{φ₁(j)} is finite); hence Q_{j,n} and q_j are measurable (Measurable.liminf). By Tonelli (Mathlib lintegral_lintegral_swap; Lebesgue measure and ν_{φ₁(j)} are σ-finite), ∫⁻_ℝ ν_{φ₁(j)}((t − h_n, t)) dt = ∫ Leb({t : x < t < x + h_n}) dν_{φ₁(j)}(x) = h_n·ν_{φ₁(j)}(ℝ), so ∫⁻_ℝ Q_{j,n} = ν_{φ₁(j)}(ℝ) ≤ Λ. Fatou's lemma (Mathlib lintegral_liminf_le) gives ∫⁻_ℝ q_j ≤ liminf_n ∫⁻_ℝ Q_{j,n} ≤ Λ for every j and, applied once more, ∫⁻_ℝ liminf_j q_j ≤ liminf_j ∫⁻_ℝ q_j ≤ Λ < ∞. Hence N₃ := {t : liminf_j q_j(t) = ∞} is Lebesgue-null (ae_lt_top).
5. (Choice of s.) The interval (a, b) has Lebesgue measure b − a > 0 and N₁ ∪ N₃ is null, so we can fix s ∈ (a, b) ∖ (N₁ ∪ N₃). Then L := liminf_j q_j(s) < ∞.
6. (Second extraction.) Since L < L + 1, q_j(s) < L + 1 for infinitely many j (Mathlib frequently_lt_of_liminf_lt), so by Mathlib extraction_of_frequently_atTop there is a strictly increasing φ₂ with q_{φ₂(k)}(s) ≤ L + 1 =: C < ∞ for every k. Put φ := φ₁ ∘ φ₂, which is strictly increasing.
7. (Proof of (i).) Fix k and let j := φ₂(k), so ν_{φ(k)} = ν_{φ₁(j)}. The sequence h_n = 1/(n + 1) tends to 0 through positive values (h_n → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0) and ENNReal.ofReal(h_n⁻¹) = n + 1. Hence, the limit inferior along the sequence (h_n) being at least the limit inferior along 𝓝[>] 0 (Mathlib Filter.Tendsto.liminf_le_liminf_comp), liminf_{h→0+} ENNReal.ofReal(h⁻¹)·ν_{φ(k)}((s − h, s)) ≤ liminf_n (n + 1)·ν_{φ(k)}((s − h_n, s)) = q_j(s) ≤ C.
8. (Proof of (ii).) Let ε ∈ (0, ∞]. If ε = ∞, any δ ∈ (0, s − a] works. Otherwise ε.toReal > 0, and since s ∉ N₁, step 3 gives δ ∈ (0, s − a] with ν_{φ₁(j)}([s − δ, s]) < ε for all large j; since φ₂(k) → ∞, ν_{φ(k)}([s − δ, s]) < ε for all large k.
By step 0, (i) and (ii) hold for μ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Restrict to [a, b]; Helly selection (Tychonoff in a countable product) gives a subsequence along which ν_j([a, d]) converges for all rational d.
At a continuity point s of the monotone limit distribution function (all but countably many s), masses of [s − δ, s] are eventually small.
Difference quotients (n + 1)·ν((t − 1/(n+1), t)) have integral ≤ Λ by Tonelli; two applications of Fatou give liminf_j q_j(t) < ∞ for a.e. t.
Choose s outside both null sets, extract a subsequence with q_j(s) bounded; (i) follows by comparing the liminf along 𝓝[>] 0 with the liminf along h_n, and (ii) from step 3.

audit.reason: Restriction makes the measures finite. Helly selection gives eventual small mass near continuity levels; Tonelli and two applications of Fatou provide finite slice majorants. The second extraction preserves the first property, and the liminf comparison has the correct direction. Both exact conclusions follow.

subproblem.title: A mass-summable series of currents defines a current (Simon Ch. 6, 7.2: the M-absolutely convergent series)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set and let X_r ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (r ∈ ℕ) be currents in U with Σ_r M(X_r) < ∞ (sum in [0, ∞]). Then there is a current Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) such that for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the real series Σ_r X_r(ω) converges to Y(ω) (HasSum), and M(Y) ≤ Σ_r M(X_r). Conventions: 𝒟_d(U) is the space of d-currents in U (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U d) and 𝒟^d(U) the test d-forms in U (TestFormOn U d: smooth forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U); |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector (covectorEuclideanNorm); M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of max(X(ω), 0) over ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (such ω are called admissible for M_G), and M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X) for X ∈ 𝒟_d(U); spt is the support of Simon 6.2.11 (GeometricCurrentOn.support); IM means integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity), an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) is the contract structure IMRep with R.measure = θ·Hⁿ⌞M, R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ (⟨ω, ξ⟩ := ξ(x)(ω(x))) and R represents X when X(ω) = R.action(ω) for all test forms ω; subtraction of currents is the contract instance Sub; X ⇀ Y is WeaklyConvergesOn.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (X : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n), ∑' r, (X r).mass ≠ ∞ → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn U n, (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, HasSum (fun r => X r ω) (Y ω)) ∧ Y.mass ≤ ∑' r, (X r).mass
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 7.2, the M-absolutely convergent series R^(ℓ) = Σ_{r≥ℓ} R_r, S^(ℓ) = Σ_{r≥ℓ} S_r (step 6 of the parent proof: "the series converge absolutely since |R_r(ω)| ≤ |ω|_∞ M(R_r) … they define currents"). Admissible below means admissible for M_U: ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (tsupport ω ⊆ U holds automatically).
1. (The norm |·|.) For an n-covector α, |α| = (Σ_I α(e_{I_1}, …, e_{I_n})²)^{1/2}, the sum over strictly increasing I : {1, …, n} → {1, …, P}. Each α ↦ α(e_{I_1}, …, e_{I_n}) is a continuous linear map, so |·| is continuous; |tα| = |t|·|α| for t ∈ ℝ, because (Σ_I (tα(e_I))²)^{1/2} = (t²·Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} = |t|·(Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (a direct consequence of the definition; SimonGMT only records the cases t = 0 and t = −1); and |α| ≤ N‖α‖ with N := (P^n)^{1/2}, ‖α‖ the operator norm of the continuous alternating map α, because |α(e_{I_1}, …, e_{I_n})| ≤ ‖α‖·Π_i ‖e_{I_i}‖ = ‖α‖ and there are at most P^n tuples I.
2. (Sup norm of a test form.) For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), x ↦ |ω(x)| is continuous (step 1) and vanishes outside the compact set tsupport ω, hence bounded; put ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_x |ω(x)| < ∞.
3. (Basic estimate.) Let X ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with M(X) < ∞, ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and c > 0 with |ω(x)| ≤ c for all x. Then |X(ω)| ≤ c·M(X)^ℝ, where M(X)^ℝ := M(X).toReal. Indeed c⁻¹ω and −c⁻¹ω belong to 𝒟ⁿ(U) (same tsupport) and |±c⁻¹ω(x)| = c⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ 1, so both are admissible; by the definition of M = M_U, ENNReal.ofReal(±c⁻¹X(ω)) ≤ M(X), i.e. ±X(ω) ≤ c·M(X)^ℝ.
4. (Definition of Y.) Put s := Σ_r M(X_r) < ∞. Then every M(X_r) is finite, the real sequence r ↦ M(X_r)^ℝ is summable (Mathlib ENNReal.summable_toReal) and Σ_r M(X_r)^ℝ = s^ℝ (ENNReal.tsum_toReal_eq). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) let c_ω := ‖ω‖_∞ + 1 > 0. By step 3, |X_r(ω)| ≤ c_ω·M(X_r)^ℝ for every r, so the real series Σ_r X_r(ω) is absolutely summable (Summable.of_norm_bounded). Define Y(ω) := Σ_r X_r(ω); thus HasSum (r ↦ X_r(ω)) (Y(ω)).
5. (Linearity.) For ω, ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and t ∈ ℝ, X_r(ω + ω') = X_r(ω) + X_r(ω') and X_r(tω) = t·X_r(ω) for every r; by HasSum.add, HasSum.mul_left and uniqueness of sums, Y(ω + ω') = Y(ω) + Y(ω') and Y(tω) = t·Y(ω). So Y is a linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U).
6. (Uniform bound.) If c > 0 and |ω(x)| ≤ c for all x, then |Y(ω)| ≤ Σ_r |X_r(ω)| ≤ Σ_r c·M(X_r)^ℝ = c·s^ℝ (steps 3 and 4).
7. (Sequential continuity.) Let ω_k → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges ω_k 0): there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω_k ⊆ K for all k and ω_k → 0 uniformly on K (the derivative of order 0; the order-0 iterated derivative has the same norm as the form). Since ω_k = 0 outside K, ε_k := sup_x ‖ω_k(x)‖ → 0, and by step 1, |ω_k(x)| ≤ N·ε_k for all x. Step 6 with c := N·ε_k + 1/(k + 1) > 0 gives |Y(ω_k)| ≤ (N·ε_k + 1/(k + 1))·s^ℝ → 0. Hence Y is sequentially continuous; together with step 5 it is a current Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and HasSum (r ↦ X_r(ω)) (Y(ω)) for every ω by step 4.
8. (Mass.) Let ω be admissible. The terms max(X_r(ω), 0) are nonnegative and dominated by |X_r(ω)|, so they are summable, and X_r(ω) ≤ max(X_r(ω), 0) termwise; hence Y(ω) = Σ_r X_r(ω) ≤ Σ_r max(X_r(ω), 0) (Mathlib Summable.tsum_le_tsum) and ENNReal.ofReal(Y(ω)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(Σ_r max(X_r(ω), 0)) = Σ_r ENNReal.ofReal(X_r(ω)) (ENNReal.ofReal_tsum_of_nonneg) ≤ Σ_r M(X_r), because ENNReal.ofReal(X_r(ω)) ≤ M(X_r) for each r (ω is admissible). Taking the supremum over admissible ω gives M(Y) ≤ Σ_r M(X_r). ∎
proof_key_steps: For |ω| ≤ c, admissibility of ±c⁻¹ω gives |X(ω)| ≤ c·M(X).
Mass-summability makes Σ_r X_r(ω) absolutely convergent; Y(ω) is its sum and is linear by uniqueness of sums.
|Y(ω)| ≤ c·Σ_r M(X_r) whenever |ω| ≤ c, and uniform convergence of ω_k → 0 gives sequential continuity.
ENNReal.ofReal(X_r(ω)) ≤ M(X_r) for admissible ω yields M(Y) ≤ Σ_r M(X_r).

subproblem.title: Extension to ℝ^P of a compactly supported integer multiplicity current in U, with mass control
subproblem.statement: Assume the following two propositions. (IR) [conjunct (b) of the frozen statement of the sibling declaration cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub] For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U and every Borel set E ⊆ ℝ^P, there are a current A ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and an IMRep R' in U with carrier M ∩ E, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ such that R' represents A. (ME) [the frozen statement of the sibling declaration cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure] For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and IMRep R in U representing T: M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P. Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, K ⊆ U compact and X ∈ 𝒟_n(U) integer multiplicity with spt X ⊆ K. Then there is an integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (a current with domain univ) whose restriction to 𝒟ⁿ(U) is X (Y.restrictDomain (subset_univ U) = X), with spt Y ⊆ K, M_{ℝ^P}(Y) ≤ M_U(X) and M_{ℝ^P}(∂Y) ≤ M_U(∂X). Conventions: 𝒟_d(U) is the space of d-currents in U (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U d) and 𝒟^d(U) the test d-forms in U (TestFormOn U d: smooth forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U); |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector (covectorEuclideanNorm); M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of max(X(ω), 0) over ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (such ω are called admissible for M_G), and M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X) for X ∈ 𝒟_d(U); spt is the support of Simon 6.2.11 (GeometricCurrentOn.support); IM means integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity), an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) is the contract structure IMRep with R.measure = θ·Hⁿ⌞M, R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ (⟨ω, ξ⟩ := ξ(x)(ω(x))) and R represents X when X(ω) = R.action(ω) for all test forms ω; subtraction of currents is the contract instance Sub; X ⇀ Y is WeaklyConvergesOn.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (E : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet E → ∃ (A : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R' : IMRep U n), R'.Represents A ∧ R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E ∧ R'.mult = R.mult ∧ R'.orient = R.orient) → (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W) → ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → IsIntegerMultiplicity X → X.support ⊆ K → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity Y ∧ Y.restrictDomain (subset_univ U) = X ∧ Y.support ⊆ K ∧ Y.mass ≤ X.mass ∧ Y.boundary.mass ≤ X.boundary.mass
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3(c) of the parent proof (extension of a current supported in the compact K ⊂ U to ℝ^P, same masses, compatible boundary, IM with the same IMRep), here built from the IMRep with (IR) instead of a cutoff formula. The sibling vanish_off_support (the accepted declaration dtc_vanish_off_support) says: Z(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ spt Z = ∅.
1. Fix an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) of X in U. U ∖ K is open (K is compact, hence closed). If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and tsupport ω ⊆ U ∖ K, then tsupport ω ∩ spt X ⊆ (U ∖ K) ∩ K = ∅, so X(ω) = 0 by vanish_off_support. Thus every value in the supremum defining M_{U∖K}(X) is ENNReal.ofReal(0) = 0, so M_{U∖K}(X) = 0, and by (ME) (U open, R represents X, U ∖ K open) R.measure(U ∖ K) = 0.
2. Since M ⊆ U, the Borel set M ∖ K is contained in U ∖ K, so ∫_{M∖K} θ dHⁿ = R.measure(M ∖ K) ≤ R.measure(U ∖ K) = 0. As θ ≥ 1 on M, Hⁿ(M ∖ K) ≤ ∫_{M∖K} θ dHⁿ = 0.
3. Apply (IR) to (U, R, E := K) (K is Borel): there is an IMRep R₁ in U with carrier M ∩ K, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ. Let R̂ be the same data (M ∩ K, θ, ξ) regarded as an IMRep in ℝ^P = univ. Every field of the structure IMRep univ n holds: M ∩ K is Borel and countably n-rectifiable, θ is measurable and positive on M ∩ K, ξ is (Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K))-a.e. strongly measurable and for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ K orients an approximate tangent space of M ∩ K at x (these fields do not involve the domain and are those of R₁); M ∩ K ⊆ univ; and for every compact K' ⊆ ℝ^P, ∫_{M∩K∩K'} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ because K is a compact subset of U and R is locally integrable in U.
4. Apply (IR) to (univ, R̂, E := univ) (univ is open): there are Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and an IMRep R̂' in ℝ^P with carrier (M ∩ K) ∩ univ = M ∩ K, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ that represents Y. Hence Y is IM and Y(ω) = ∫_{M∩K} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P).
5. (Restriction.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); as a form it belongs to 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (testFormOnInclusion). By step 4 and Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 (step 2; the sets M ∩ K and M differ by an Hⁿ-null set, Mathlib setIntegral_congr_set), Y(ω) = ∫_{M∩K} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = X(ω), the last equality because R represents X. So (Y.restrictDomain (subset_univ U))(ω) = Y(ω) = X(ω) for every ω, i.e. Y.restrictDomain (subset_univ U) = X (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
6. (Support.) Let x ∈ ℝ^P ∖ K. As K is closed there is r > 0 with closedBall(x, r) ∩ K = ∅. V := ball(x, r) is open with compact closure (contained in closedBall(x, r)) in ℝ^P. If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) and tsupport ω ⊆ V, then ω = 0 on K ⊇ M ∩ K, so Y(ω) = 0 by step 4. Hence V lies in the zero region of Y and x ∉ spt Y. Therefore spt Y ⊆ K.
7. (Mass.) By (ME) in ℝ^P (univ is open and R̂' represents Y), M(Y) = M_{ℝ^P}(Y) = R̂'.measure(ℝ^P) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ = R.measure(K) ≤ R.measure(U) = M_U(X) = M(X), the last two equalities by (ME) in U with W := U.
8. (Boundary mass.) By Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open choose δ > 0 with K_δ := cthickening(δ, K) ⊆ U; K_δ is compact. By Mathlib exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior (closed set K, t := K_δ, K ⊆ thickening(δ, K) ⊆ interior K_δ) (with smoothness index ∞, converted to ContDiff ℝ ∞ by contMDiff_iff_contDiff) there is a smooth ζ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] that equals 1 on an open set V ⊇ K and vanishes outside K_δ; so tsupport ζ ⊆ K_δ is compact and contained in U. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) be admissible for M_{ℝ^P}(∂Y), i.e. |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. Then ζω is smooth with tsupport contained in K_δ, so ζω ∈ 𝒟^m(U), and |ζ(x)ω(x)| = ζ(x)|ω(x)| ≤ 1, so ζω is admissible for M_U(∂X). On the open set V, ζω = ω, so d(ζω) = dω on V (the exterior derivative at a point only depends on the form near that point), in particular on M ∩ K ⊆ K ⊆ V. Using step 4 for dω and d(ζω) (both in 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P)) and step 5 for d(ζω) ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U):
 ∂Y(ω) = Y(dω) = ∫_{M∩K} θ⟨dω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_{M∩K} θ⟨d(ζω), ξ⟩ dHⁿ = Y(d(ζω)) = X(d(ζω)) = ∂X(ζω).
 Hence ENNReal.ofReal(∂Y(ω)) = ENNReal.ofReal(∂X(ζω)) ≤ M_U(∂X). Taking the supremum over admissible ω gives M(∂Y) ≤ M(∂X). ∎
proof_key_steps: spt X ⊆ K gives M_{U∖K}(X) = 0 (vanish_off_support), so by (ME) the carrier of an IMRep of X is Hⁿ-null outside K.
Restrict the carrier to K with (IR), read the data as an IMRep in ℝ^P and take the current Y it represents (again (IR)).
Y restricts to X on 𝒟ⁿ(U), vanishes away from K, and M(Y) = R.measure(K) ≤ M(X) by (ME).
A smooth cutoff ζ = 1 near K gives ∂Y(ω) = ∂X(ζω), hence M(∂Y) ≤ M(∂X).

subproblem.title: Localization of a weakly convergent integer multiplicity sequence near closure(W) (Simon Ch. 6, 7.2, (4))
subproblem.statement: Assume the following five propositions. (SL) [the frozen statement of the sibling declaration cmc_slice_mass_bounds] For all P, k ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), Borel measures μ, μ' on ℝ^P that are finite on compact subsets of U, maps ξ (to (k+1)-vectors) and ξ' (to k-vectors) that are μ- resp. μ'-a.e. strongly measurable such that for μ-a.e. x, |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every (k+1)-covector α, for μ'-a.e. x, |⟨α, ξ'(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every k-covector α, T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ for ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U) and ∂T(η) = ∫⟨η, ξ'⟩ dμ' for η ∈ 𝒟^k(U), and every L-Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ (L ∈ [0, ∞)), there are currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), B_t ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}⟨η, ξ'⟩ dμ', ∂A_t(η) = B_t(η) whenever tsupport η misses {f = t}, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} ENNReal.ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for every open W and t, and ∫⁻_{(a,b)} M_W(∂A_t − B_t) dt ≤ L·μ(W ∩ {a < f < b}) for every open W and a, b. (BR) [the second conjunct of the frozen statement of cmc_closure_and_boundary_rectifiability] For all P, d ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and every IM R ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) with M_V(∂R) < ∞ for every open V with closure(V) compact and contained in U, the boundary ∂R is IM. (IR) [conjunct (b) of the frozen statement of the sibling declaration cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub] For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U and every Borel set E ⊆ ℝ^P, there are a current A ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and an IMRep R' in U with carrier M ∩ E, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ such that R' represents A. (IO) [conjunct (d) of the frozen statement of cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub] For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every U ⊆ ℝ^P and every IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α. (ME) [the frozen statement of the sibling declaration cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure] For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and IMRep R in U representing T: M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P. Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let T_j (j ∈ ℕ) and T be integer multiplicity currents in 𝒟_n(U) with sup_j (M_V(T_j) + M_V(∂T_j)) < ∞ for every open V with closure(V) compact and contained in U, and T_j ⇀ T in U, and let W ⊆ ℝ^P with closure(W) compact and contained in U. Then there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ, a compact K ⊆ U, Λ ∈ [0, ∞) and integer multiplicity T'_j (j ∈ ℕ), T' ∈ 𝒟_n(U) such that for every j: spt T'_j ⊆ K, M(T'_j) ≤ Λ and M(∂T'_j) ≤ Λ; T'_j ⇀ T' in U; and T'_j(ω) = T_{φ(j)}(ω) and T'(ω) = T(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Conventions: 𝒟_d(U) is the space of d-currents in U (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U d) and 𝒟^d(U) the test d-forms in U (TestFormOn U d: smooth forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U); |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector (covectorEuclideanNorm); M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of max(X(ω), 0) over ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (such ω are called admissible for M_G), and M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X) for X ∈ 𝒟_d(U); spt is the support of Simon 6.2.11 (GeometricCurrentOn.support); IM means integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity), an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) is the contract structure IMRep with R.measure = θ·Hⁿ⌞M, R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ (⟨ω, ξ⟩ := ξ(x)(ω(x))) and R represents X when X(ω) = R.action(ω) for all test forms ω; subtraction of currents is the contract instance Sub; X ⇀ Y is WeaklyConvergesOn.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 (with step 2) of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 7.2, (4): "by 4.5(1),(2) and an argument as in 6.7(2) of Ch. 2 we can find a subsequence … such that sup_j M(∂(T_j⌞W_i)) < ∞", together with the weak convergence of the localized currents, which the parent proof obtains from the absence of limiting mass on the slicing level. Notation: for an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U, R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M; ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_x |ω(x)| < ∞ for a test form ω (continuous with compact support); M := M_U.
Facts about an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U representing a current Z ∈ 𝒟_d(U):
(R1) R.measure(K₁) = ∫_{M∩K₁} θ dH^d < ∞ for compact K₁ ⊆ U (field locallyIntegrable_mult).
(R2) Z(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dR.measure for ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U): R.measure = (H^d⌞M).withDensity θ with θ measurable, so ∫ f dR.measure = ∫_M θ f dH^d (Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul for the ℝ≥0-valued θ), and Z(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^d.
(R3) For R.measure-a.e. x, |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every d-covector α: (IO) gives this for H^d⌞M-a.e. x, and R.measure ≪ H^d⌞M (Mathlib withDensity_absolutelyContinuous). Consequently, for ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) and Borel B with R.measure(B) < ∞, the function f(x) := ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ is R.measure-a.e. strongly measurable (R4; ω is continuous and evaluation is continuous) with |f| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞ R.measure-a.e., hence integrable on B (Mathlib Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded / IntegrableOn.of_bound), |∫_B f dR.measure| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞·R.measure(B).toReal, and if |ω| ≤ 1 everywhere then ∫_B f dR.measure ≤ R.measure(B).toReal; the same holds for χf with any measurable χ with values in [0, 1].
(R4) ξ is R.measure-a.e. strongly measurable (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient and absolute continuity, AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac).
(R5) M_V(Z) = R.measure(V) for open V (ME).
(R6) For Borel E, (IR) gives a current Z⌞E ∈ 𝒟_d(U) represented by an IMRep with carrier M ∩ E, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ; its measure is R.measure⌞E, because (H^d⌞(M ∩ E)).withDensity θ = ((H^d⌞M).withDensity θ)⌞E. By (R2), Z⌞E(ω) = ∫_E⟨ω, ξ⟩ dR.measure; in particular Z⌞E is IM.
0. (Case W = ∅.) Take φ := id, K := ∅, Λ := 0 and T'_j := T' := T⌞∅ (R6 with E := ∅). By (R6), T⌞∅(ω) = 0 for every ω, so T⌞∅ = 0: it is IM; its support is empty (each x ∈ U has a ball with compact closure in U, U being open, on which it vanishes); its mass and the mass of its boundary (the zero current) are 0; the constant sequence converges weakly; and a form with tsupport ⊆ ∅ is identically 0, so T'_j(ω) = 0 = T_j(ω) and T'(ω) = 0 = T(ω) by linearity. From now on W ≠ ∅.
1. (Geometry.) C := closure(W) is nonempty, compact and contained in U. By Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open there is δ₀ > 0 with cthickening(δ₀, C) ⊆ U; put δ := δ₀/3, so cthickening(3δ, C) ⊆ U. Let g(x) := infDist(x, C); g is 1-Lipschitz (Mathlib lipschitz_infDist_pt), continuous, and g = 0 on C ⊇ W. Since C ≠ ∅, infEDist(x, C) = ENNReal.ofReal(infDist(x, C)) (infEDist(x, C) ≠ ∞ for nonempty C, Mathlib Metric.infEDist_ne_top), so for 0 ≤ r the set {g ≤ r} equals cthickening(r, C) = {x : infEDist(x, C) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(r)}; it is closed (g is continuous) and bounded (C is bounded), hence compact, and for r ≤ 3δ it is contained in cthickening(3δ, C) ⊆ U. W₁ := {g < 5δ/2} is open with closure(W₁) ⊆ {g ≤ 5δ/2}, compact and contained in U. By hypothesis Λ₀ := sup_j (M_{W₁}(T_j) + M_{W₁}(∂T_j)) < ∞.
2. (Representations.) For each j fix an IMRep R_j = (M_j, θ_j, ξ_j) of T_j. For every open V with closure(V) compact and contained in U, M_V(∂T_j) ≤ sup_i (M_V(T_i) + M_V(∂T_i)) < ∞, so ∂T_j is IM by (BR); fix an IMRep R'_j = (M'_j, θ'_j, ξ'_j) of ∂T_j. Fix an IMRep R_T of T. Put μ_j := R_j.measure, μ'_j := R'_j.measure and μ_T := R_T.measure.
3. (Slicing.) For each j apply (SL) with k := m, T := T_j, (μ, ξ) := (μ_j, ξ_j), (μ', ξ') := (μ'_j, ξ'_j), f := g and L := 1. Its hypotheses hold by (R1)–(R4) for R_j and for R'_j (which represents ∂T_j) and because g is 1-Lipschitz. It yields A_j(t) ∈ 𝒟_n(U), B_j(t) ∈ 𝒟_m(U) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_j(t)(ω) = ∫_{g<t}⟨ω, ξ_j⟩ dμ_j and B_j(t)(η) = ∫_{g<t}⟨η, ξ'_j⟩ dμ'_j, and, for Z_j(t) := ∂A_j(t) − B_j(t), every open V and every t: M_V(Z_j(t)) ≤ liminf_{h→0+} ENNReal.ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ_j(V ∩ {t − h < g < t}).
4. (Good level.) Let λ_j := μ_j.map g, a Borel measure on ℝ (g is continuous, hence measurable) with λ_j(E) = μ_j(g⁻¹(E)) for Borel E. Since {δ ≤ g ≤ 2δ} ⊆ W₁, λ_j([δ, 2δ]) ≤ μ_j(W₁) = M_{W₁}(T_j) ≤ Λ₀ (R5). The sibling good_slice with a := δ, b := 2δ and Λ := Λ₀ gives s ∈ (δ, 2δ), a strictly increasing φ and C₁ ∈ [0, ∞) such that (i) liminf_{h→0+} ENNReal.ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ_{φ(j)}({s − h < g < s}) ≤ C₁ for every j, and (ii) for every ε > 0 there is δ_ε > 0 with μ_{φ(j)}({s − δ_ε ≤ g ≤ s}) ≤ ε for all large j.
5. (Definitions.) G := {g < s} is open, W ⊆ C ⊆ G and G ⊆ W₁; K := {g ≤ s} is compact, K ⊆ U and G ⊆ K. Put T'_j := A_{φ(j)}(s), T' := T⌞G (R6 with E := G) and Λ := (Λ₀ + C₁).toNNReal, so that Λ = Λ₀ + C₁ in [0, ∞].
6. (IM.) T' is IM by (R6). By (R6) for R_{φ(j)} and E := G, T_{φ(j)}⌞G(ω) = ∫_G⟨ω, ξ_{φ(j)}⟩ dμ_{φ(j)} = T'_j(ω) for every ω, so T'_j = T_{φ(j)}⌞G is IM.
7. (Support.) Let x ∈ U ∖ K, so g(x) > s. The open set U ∩ {g > s} contains x; choose r > 0 with closedBall(x, r) ⊆ U ∩ {g > s}. V := ball(x, r) is open with compact closure contained in U, and V ∩ G = ∅. If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and tsupport ω ⊆ V, then ω = 0 on G and T'_j(ω) = ∫_G⟨ω, ξ_{φ(j)}⟩ dμ_{φ(j)} = 0. So V lies in the zero region of T'_j and x ∉ spt T'_j; as spt T'_j ⊆ U by definition, spt T'_j ⊆ K.
8. (Mass bounds.) (a) If ω is admissible for M_U (|ω| ≤ 1), then T'_j(ω) = ∫_G⟨ω, ξ_{φ(j)}⟩ dμ_{φ(j)} ≤ μ_{φ(j)}(G) by (R3); hence M(T'_j) ≤ μ_{φ(j)}(G) ≤ μ_{φ(j)}(W₁) = M_{W₁}(T_{φ(j)}) ≤ Λ₀ ≤ Λ (R5). (b) In the same way M(B_{φ(j)}(s)) ≤ μ'_{φ(j)}(G) ≤ μ'_{φ(j)}(W₁) = M_{W₁}(∂T_{φ(j)}) ≤ Λ₀ (R3 and R5 for R'_{φ(j)}). By step 3 with V := ℝ^P and by (i), M(Z_{φ(j)}(s)) = M_U(Z_{φ(j)}(s)) ≤ M_{ℝ^P}(Z_{φ(j)}(s)) ≤ liminf_{h→0+} ENNReal.ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ_{φ(j)}(ℝ^P ∩ {s − h < g < s}) ≤ C₁ (mass is monotone in the region). Since ∂T'_j(η) = B_{φ(j)}(s)(η) + Z_{φ(j)}(s)(η) for all η, for admissible η we get ENNReal.ofReal(∂T'_j(η)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(B_{φ(j)}(s)(η)) + ENNReal.ofReal(Z_{φ(j)}(s)(η)) ≤ M(B_{φ(j)}(s)) + M(Z_{φ(j)}(s)); hence M(∂T'_j) ≤ Λ₀ + C₁ = Λ.
9. (Agreement on W.) If tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ G, then ω = 0 outside G, so T'_j(ω) = ∫_G⟨ω, ξ_{φ(j)}⟩ dμ_{φ(j)} = ∫⟨ω, ξ_{φ(j)}⟩ dμ_{φ(j)} = T_{φ(j)}(ω) by (R2); likewise T'(ω) = ∫_G⟨ω, ξ_T⟩ dμ_T = T(ω).
10. (Weak convergence.) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), put c := ‖ω‖_∞ and let ε ∈ (0, ∞). The sets {s − 1/(i+1) < g < s} decrease to ∅ and μ_T(G) ≤ μ_T(K) < ∞ (R1), so by continuity from above there is δ₁ > 0 with μ_T({s − δ₁ < g < s}) ≤ ε. By (ii) there is δ₂ > 0 with μ_{φ(j)}({s − δ₂ ≤ g ≤ s}) ≤ ε for all large j. Let δ' := min(δ₁, δ₂, s/2) > 0. By Mathlib exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior (closed set {g ≤ s − δ'}, t := {g ≤ s − δ'/2}, whose interior contains the open set {g < s − δ'/2} ⊇ {g ≤ s − δ'}) there is a smooth χ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with χ = 1 on {g ≤ s − δ'} and χ = 0 outside {g ≤ s − δ'/2}; then tsupport χ ⊆ {g ≤ s − δ'/2}, which is compact and contained in G ⊆ U, so χω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). By (R3) the functions ⟨ω, ξ_{φ(j)}⟩ and χ⟨ω, ξ_{φ(j)}⟩ are μ_{φ(j)}-integrable on G (bounded by c a.e., μ_{φ(j)}(G) ≤ μ_{φ(j)}(K) < ∞ by (R1)), and the same holds for μ_T, so the integrals below may be split linearly. Since χ = 0 outside G, (R2) gives T_{φ(j)}(χω) = ∫_G χ⟨ω, ξ_{φ(j)}⟩ dμ_{φ(j)}, hence T'_j(ω) − T_{φ(j)}(χω) = ∫_G (1 − χ)⟨ω, ξ_{φ(j)}⟩ dμ_{φ(j)}; the integrand vanishes on {g ≤ s − δ'} and has absolute value ≤ c for μ_{φ(j)}-a.e. x (R3). Thus |T'_j(ω) − T_{φ(j)}(χω)| ≤ c·μ_{φ(j)}({s − δ' < g < s}) ≤ c·μ_{φ(j)}({s − δ₂ ≤ g ≤ s}) ≤ cε for all large j, and likewise |T'(ω) − T(χω)| ≤ c·μ_T({s − δ' < g < s}) ≤ c·μ_T({s − δ₁ < g < s}) ≤ cε. Since T_{φ(j)}(χω) → T(χω) (T_j ⇀ T and φ(j) → ∞), limsup_j |T'_j(ω) − T'(ω)| ≤ 2cε. As ε > 0 was arbitrary, T'_j(ω) → T'(ω); hence T'_j ⇀ T' in U.
11. The data φ, K, Λ, (T'_j)_j and T' satisfy all requirements (steps 5–10). ∎
proof_key_steps: IMReps of T_j, of ∂T_j (IM by (BR)) and of T give measures with |ξ| ≤ 1 a.e. (IO) and M_V = measure on open V (ME), as required by (SL).

Slicing by g = dist(·, closure W) gives T_j⌞{g < t}, (∂T_j)⌞{g < t} and pointwise slice-mass bounds; the sibling good_slice picks s ∈ (δ, 2δ) and a subsequence with bounded slice masses and no limiting mass concentration at {g = s}.
T'_j := T_{φ(j)}⌞{g < s} and T' := T⌞{g < s} are IM (IR), supported in {g ≤ s}, have M(T'_j) ≤ Λ₀ and M(∂T'_j) ≤ Λ₀ + C₁, and agree with T_{φ(j)}, T on forms supported in W.
A cutoff χ = 1 on {g ≤ s − δ'} and the no-concentration bound give T'_j ⇀ T'.

audit.reason: All five prerequisites are explicit; neither prose nor type requires W open. 3. (Telescoping.) For every N, X_{ℓ+N+1} − X_ℓ − S^N = ∂R^N. For N = 0 this is the hypothesis at r = ℓ. For every N: M_G(R^N) ≤ 2; by step 3 and (F1), M_G(∂R^N) = M_G(X_{ℓ+N+1} − X_ℓ − S^N) ≤ M(X_{ℓ+N+1}) + M(X_ℓ) + M(S^N) ≤ 2Λ + 2; M_G(S^N) ≤ 2; and M_G(∂S^N) ≤ 2Λ by step 4. Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 7.2, the total boundedness (1) derived from the deformation theorem in (2), (3); step 4 of the parent proof, carried out for currents in U through the extension to ℝ^P and restriction back to U (step 3(c) and step 7 of the parent proof). Two elementary facts:
(F1) Mass subadditivity: for currents A, B with the same domain and every set G, M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B). Indeed, if ω is admissible for M_G then so is −ω, (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) + B(−ω), and ENNReal.ofReal(s + t) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(s) + ENNReal.ofReal(t); take the supremum over ω.
(F2) Restriction to U. For Z ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) write Z|_U := Z.restrictDomain (subset_univ U); then Z|_U(ω) = Z(ω) for ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) (regarded in 𝒟^d(ℝ^P)), (A − B)|_U = A|_U − B|_U, and M_U(Z|_U) ≤ M_{ℝ^P}(Z), since every form admissible for M_U(Z|_U) is admissible for M_{ℝ^P}(Z) with the same value. If Z is IM, so is Z|_U: let (M_Z, θ_Z, ξ_Z) be an IMRep of Z; (IR) in ℝ^P with E := U (open, hence Borel) gives an IMRep in ℝ^P with carrier M_Z ∩ U, multiplicity θ_Z and orientation ξ_Z. The same data form an IMRep in U (the carrier lies in U, local integrability over compact subsets of U is a special case of local integrability over all compact sets, and the remaining fields do not involve the domain), and it represents Z|_U: every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) vanishes outside U, so ∫_{M_Z∩U} θ_Z⟨ω, ξ_Z⟩ dH^d = ∫_{M_Z} θ_Z⟨ω, ξ_Z⟩ dH^d = Z(ω) = Z|_U(ω).
1. Let c ≥ 1 be the constant given by (DF) for (P, m). Choose ρ > 0 with 2c·ρ·Λ ≤ η: ρ := 1 if η = ∞, and ρ := η.toReal/(2c(Λ + 1)) otherwise (then 2cρΛ = η.toReal·Λ/(Λ + 1) ≤ η.toReal, so in [0, ∞] the inequality c·ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)·Λ + c·ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)·Λ ≤ η holds).
2. Apply (DF) to (ρ, K, Λ): there is a finite set 𝒬̂ ⊆ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with the deformation property. Let 𝒬 := {Q̂|_U : Q̂ ∈ 𝒬̂}, finite as the image of a finite set.
3. Let X ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) be IM with spt X ⊆ K, M(X) ≤ Λ and M(∂X) ≤ Λ. The sibling extend_to_univ (applied with the assumed (IR) and (ME)) gives an IM Y ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with Y|_U = X, spt Y ⊆ K, M(Y) ≤ M(X) ≤ Λ and M(∂Y) ≤ M(∂X) ≤ Λ < ∞. By (DF) there are Q̂ ∈ 𝒬̂, R̂ ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) and Ŝ ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with Q̂ and R̂ IM, Y − Q̂ − Ŝ = ∂R̂, M(Q̂) ≤ c·M(Y) ≤ cΛ, M(R̂) ≤ cρ·M(Y) ≤ cρΛ and M(Ŝ) ≤ cρ·M(∂Y) ≤ cρΛ.
4. (Ŝ is IM.) By (F1), M(∂R̂) = M(Y − Q̂ − Ŝ) ≤ M(Y) + M(Q̂) + M(Ŝ) ≤ Λ + cΛ + cρΛ < ∞, so M_G(∂R̂) ≤ M(∂R̂) < ∞ for every open G (mass is monotone in the region). By (BR) applied with U := ℝ^P (open), d := m + 1 and the IM current R̂ ∈ 𝒟_{(m+1)+1}(ℝ^P), ∂R̂ is IM. Evaluating Y − Q̂ − Ŝ = ∂R̂ at any ω gives Ŝ(ω) = Y(ω) − Q̂(ω) − ∂R̂(ω), i.e. Ŝ = (Y − Q̂) − ∂R̂, which is IM by (IS) applied twice.
5. Put Q := Q̂|_U ∈ 𝒬, R := R̂|_U and S := Ŝ|_U; R and S are IM by (F2). For ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U), dω ∈ 𝒟^{m+2}(U) and (X − Q − S)(ω) = Y(ω) − Q̂(ω) − Ŝ(ω) = ∂R̂(ω) = R̂(dω) = R(dω) = ∂R(ω), using Y|_U = X. Hence X − Q − S = ∂R.
6. By (F2), M(R) + M(S) ≤ M(R̂) + M(Ŝ) ≤ 2cρΛ ≤ η. ∎
proof_key_steps: Fix ρ with 2cρΛ ≤ η and the finite family 𝒬̂ of (DF) for (ρ, K, Λ); 𝒬 is the set of its restrictions to U.
Extend X to Y on ℝ^P (sibling extend_to_univ) and deform: Y − Q̂ − Ŝ = ∂R̂ with M(R̂), M(Ŝ) ≤ cρΛ.
∂R̂ has finite mass, so it is IM by (BR), and Ŝ = (Y − Q̂) − ∂R̂ is IM by (IS).
Restricting Q̂, R̂, Ŝ to U preserves IM (via (IR)), the identity and the mass bounds.

audit.reason: The five antecedents match the frozen prerequisites. Extension permits deformation against one finite family; finite boundary mass justifies BR before asserting that the remainder is IM. Domain restriction preserves the identity, IM property and mass estimates, giving precisely the stated conclusion.
